# MouseOS

> MouseOS turns an Android phone into a wireless trackpad, air mouse, keyboard, media remote and presentation clicker for a Mac, a Windows PC or a Linux computer — and into a remote for Samsung, LG and Google TVs. It is free for the basics and works over the local Wi‑Fi (the internet is needed only to sign in once), with no cloud, no ads and no tracking. Website: https://mouseos.app/

## Facts

- Name: MouseOS (on Google Play: "MouseOS — Mac, PC & TV Remote")
- Price: the basics are free, with no ads: trackpad, air mouse, keyboard, remote, TV, copy-paste, shortcuts, slides (next, back, black screen), one computer and one TV. MouseOS Pro, bought in the phone app, adds several computers and TVs, the slides timer, notes, drawing and laser pointer, keeping the computer awake, and the Bluetooth mouse mode: €7.99 a year with a 7-day free trial, or €1.99 a month. The computer app and the browser helper are free. The phone app asks for a free MouseOS account (email and password, or Google), which can be deleted in one tap.
- Phone app: Android 8 or later. In closed beta on Google Play: join at https://mouseos.app/#beta with a Google account email, get added to the test, install from Google Play. iPhone: on the way.
- Computer app (free, required for computers, not for TVs): macOS 11 or later on Apple silicon (.dmg), Windows 10 and 11 64‑bit (.msi), Linux 64‑bit on X11 or Wayland (.deb for Ubuntu/Debian/Mint, .rpm for Fedora/openSUSE). Downloads: https://github.com/MathisZerbib/mouseos/releases/latest
- TVs: Samsung, LG and Google TV (Sony, TCL, Philips…), controlled straight from the phone over the same Wi‑Fi.
- The six screens: PAD (trackpad: tap to click, two‑finger scroll or scroll strip, hold to drag), AIR (air mouse: aim the phone like a TV remote, gyroscope), REMOTE (arrows, play/pause, the computer's volume, next episode), TV, KEYS (keyboard in any language, accents and emoji), SLIDES (presentation clicker: giant next/previous, the volume buttons click; talk timer with Pro).
- Connection: the phone and the computer talk directly over the local Wi‑Fi network, or over the phone's hotspot. No server: the internet is needed only to sign in once. The computer finds the phone by itself; each new phone is approved once with one ALLOW click on the computer.
- Privacy: no cloud, no advertising SDK. What you do never leaves your network. The apps send anonymous usage counts (PostHog, can be turned off) and crash reports; the account (email address) is kept in the EU. Policy: https://mouseos.app/privacy-policy.html · Terms: https://mouseos.app/terms.html
- Version: 2.21.0 (November 2026).
- Developer: Mathis Zerbib, independent. Contact: support@mouseos.app
- Languages: the site is in English at https://mouseos.app/ and in French (/fr/), Portuguese (/pt/), Spanish (/es/), German (/de/), Italian (/it/), Japanese (/ja/) and Chinese (/zh/) — the same pages, each at that path.

## Setup in short

1. On the computer: install the free MouseOS companion app and allow it to control the pointer (macOS: Privacy & Security → Accessibility; Linux on Wayland: click ALLOW CONTROL; Windows: allow network access on a Private network).
2. On the phone: open MouseOS on the same Wi‑Fi. It finds the computer by itself.
3. On the computer: click ALLOW once for that phone. Done.

- [Phone as a presentation clicker](https://mouseos.app/presentation-remote.html): Keynote, PowerPoint, Google Slides; volume buttons turn slides, a talk timer with MouseOS Pro
- [Phone as a TV remote](https://mouseos.app/tv-remote.html): Samsung, LG and Google TV over Wi‑Fi, pairing for each
- [Linux, X11 and Wayland](https://mouseos.app/linux-remote-mouse.html): how input works on each session (XTest, uinput), ports, packages
- [MouseOS and other remote apps](https://mouseos.app/alternatives.html): what it does differently from Unified Remote, Remote Mouse and KDE Connect, and when they fit better
